messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High KV cache eviction and continuous-batch queue growth detected on prod-us-west-2 at 08:12 UTC — svc=runtime shard=kv-28 metric=eviction_rate metric_value=8.7k/min :rotating_light:
eli_oncall: acked. paging @maya_sre and @ryan_runtime. I'm on call, looking now.
maya_sre: seeing large tail latency on Llama-backed endpoints. 95th p90->p99 jump. also prefetch miss-rate up. attaching quick grafana link: https://grafana/reds/alert/3123
ryan_runtime: logs show continuous_batch queue backlog rising and KV cache working set exploded for mixed-model traffic. suspect prefetch loop hitting high-cardinality prefixes from Qwen->Mistral transition.
anya_ml: can you dump model-routing headers? trying to see if requests were routed to model variants unexpectedly after a rollout.
eli_oncall: retrieving routing headers...
eli_oncall: ```json
{
  "route": "mixflow-v2",
  "model_chain": ["qwen-1.0", "mistral-0.9", "llama-2-13b"],
  "prefetch_policy": "aggressive"
}
```
maya_sre: aha — mixflow-v2 aggressive prefetch enabled yesterday via canary. looks like it didn't respect prefix cardinality threshold. high prefix cardinality caused KV cache blowup (~3.2x expected memory).
jord_support: any user impact? Customer IOPS spike reported by tenant-42, they say increased latency and some 5xx between 08:10-08:30 UTC.
ryan_runtime: confirmed: tenant-42 and a few other high-concurrency customers saw timeouts and elevated retry rates. We automatically degraded a subset of requests to CPU fallback (latency > 2s), which increased downstream errors. Not a data loss but user-facing timeouts.
eli_oncall: quick mitigation: flip prefetch_policy to conservative for mixflow-v2 on prod-us-west-2. Maya, can SRE push the hotfix to routing config?
maya_sre: I can patch. preparing a safe canary rollback for prefetch flag.
maya_sre: ```bash
# patch route policy to conservative prefetch
curl -X POST https://controlplane/api/routes/mixflow-v2/policy -d '{"prefetch_policy":"conservative","prefetch_cardinality_threshold":1000}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```
release-bot: deploy started: route-policy-mixflowv2-20260315T08:20Z by maya_sre. CI checks passed.
ryan_runtime: while that goes out, enable extra KV eviction guard and throttle continuous-batching to short windows to avoid queue accumulation.
maya_sre: applying KV guard: ```yaml
kvgc:
  max_active_keys: 200000
  eviction_ratio: 0.15
  aggressive_eviction: true
```
release-bot: KV guard applied on kv-28, kv-29, kv-30.
eli_oncall: monitoring. p50 improved immediately, p95 trending down. backlog length dropping.
anya_ml: note: the aggressive prefetch combined with model-chain routing produced duplicate cached entries per model variant (qwen vs mistral) because prefix normalization wasn't canonicalized across model names. that's why memory increased so much. We should normalize keys in prefetch to include canonical model family, not variant.
ryan_runtime: agree — short term: conservative policy + eviction guard. medium term: fix prefix canonicalization and add cardinality guard in prefetcher. I'll open an RFC.
jord_support: informing tenant-42 that we mitigated and latency is improving. drafting message: "We observed a prefetch-induced cache pressure event affecting latency for your requests; we've rolled back the aggressive prefetch policy and are monitoring — please reach out if you still see issues"
eli_oncall: Next: can we identify if any rollout triggered this? anya, any recent canaries touching mixflow-v2?
anya_ml: mixflow-v2 was promoted canary->100% at 03:40 UTC yesterday, but conservative->aggressive prefetch toggle was flipped in staged config at 01:15 UTC CI job 452. Might've been missed in QA for high-card scenarios.
maya_sre: I want to add a safety net: reject prefetch policies that set aggressive for routes flagged high-card. adding policy check to control plane.
ray_monitor: (bot) metric: continuous_batch_queue_length for kv-28 dropped from 18k to 900 at 08:28 UTC. eviction_rate normalized.
eli_oncall: good. last check: any residual errors?
ryan_runtime: a small cohort still hitting p99 tail for Llama endpoints due to KV key churn. starting a targeted warmup of common prefixes for tenant-42 to prevent cold misses.
anya_ml: for the canonicalization fix, propose: normalize prefix by (normalize_text(prefix) + model_family) instead of model_variant. should reduce duplication across qwen/mistral/llama families.
maya_sre: timeline: hotfix to control plane policy (reject aggressive on high-card) -> follow-up RFC and code change to prefetcher for canonicalization -> automated regression test with high-prefix-cardinality sim.
eli_oncall: customer comms sent by Jord. I'll leave this for monitoring window. handing off to @maya_sre for follow-up. summarize handoff pls.
maya_sre: Handoff summary: incident-id=INC-2026-03-mixflow-prefetch-01; impact: elevated latency and intermittent 5xx for high-concurrency tenants (tenant-42 etc) between 08:10-08:30 UTC. Root cause: aggressive prefetch + missing prefix canonicalization + route promotion of mixflow-v2. Immediate mitigations: reverted prefetch to conservative, applied KV eviction guard, throttled continuous-batching. Current status: stabilized, p95 trending to baseline, monitoring for 1h. Next steps: patch prefetcher canonicalization, add control plane policy check, add regression test. Owners: maya_sre (policy), ryan_runtime (prefetcher fix), anya_ml (model routing review).
eli_oncall: thanks. ending pager. :white_check_mark:
release-bot: deploy complete: route-policy-mixflowv2-20260315T08:20Z — status=success.
maya_sre: logging incident record and sending notes to postmortems channel.
jord_support: customer update posted to tenant-42. they replied: "Thanks, seeing improvements, will keep you posted." :thumbsup:
eli_oncall: closing thread, will reopen if metrics regress.
